title: introduce-canonical-output-sanitizer-and-stream-coercion-fallback
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: production services using response_format=strict were observing two classes of failures: 1) streaming outputs that transiently emitted extra/unexpected keys mid-stream and then corrected themselves, causing downstream JSONschema validation to fail; 2) toolcall/tool payloads that contained large opaque blobs or PII which should not be indiscriminately surfaced to downstream tooling when strict enforcement is enabled. This PR introduces a canonical output sanitizer plus a stream-coercion fallback path to make strict schema enforcement robust for long-running streaming responses while preserving OpenAI-compat semantics. Changes: - runtime: add canonicalizer that prunes fields not present in the declared JSON Schema for the route and normalizes field ordering to produce consistent snapshots for checkpoint validation. - streaming: introduce schema-checkpoint events (stream_checkpoint.v1) that carry compacted canonical snapshots and a pass/fail hint so the client can resume or anchor parsing without re-sending the full token buffer. - fallback: when strict mode is configured with "coercion:soft-fallback", the runtime will attempt best-effort coercion (type coercion, null-to-empty defaults, string trimming) for transient violations and emit a structured diagnostic instead of immediately terminating the stream. - toolcall safety: implement opaque-tool-token substitution for tool payloads when route config sets "tool_payload_mode":"opaque_on_strict"; actual payloads are retained in a secure KVS accessible to authorized workers for replay, reducing leakage risk in public logs or downstream tool adapters. - openai-compat: compat adapter returns a 400 with a standardized diagnostic JSON (diagnostic_id, code, human_message, hints) for hard schema violations; soft-fallbacks surface via a non-2xx streaming meta event rather than drop the connection. - config: new top-level response_format.contract_safety config with options {strict, permissive, strict_with_coercion, strict_with_opaque_tooling}. - telemetry & observability: add counters and sample histograms for schema.validation.duration, schema.validation.failures_by_code, stream.checkpoint.bytes, tool.opaque_replacements. - docs & SDK: update OpenAPI examples and python/ts SDK quickstarts for route-level response_format and migration notes. Backwards compatibility: default behavior remains unchanged for routes without explicit response_format.contract_safety. For routes that opt into the new strict_with_opaque_tooling mode, the change is additive and documented. Testing: unit tests for canonicalizer, end-to-end streaming fixture that simulates mid-stream schema transients, security test for KVS access control. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout in three phases (internal dogfood, opt-in beta, on-by-default after telemetry review). Checklist: - [x] core runtime sanitizer implementation - [x] streaming checkpoint protocol - [x] OpenAI compat diagnostic mapping - [x] SDK + docs updates - [x] unit and e2e tests - [x] telemetry events instrumented Related: ENG-4829 (schema stability initiative), SUP-1289 (customer incident report), ENG-4901 (tooling safety audit).

release_notes: Add a canonical output sanitizer and stream-coercion fallback to improve reliability of response_format=strict; new route-level contract_safety options and safer handling of tool payloads in strict modes. Backwards compatible unless opted in.
notes_on_migration: If you are using response_format=strict and rely on immediate hard termination on the first schema mismatch, audit routes that will be toggled to strict_with_coercion or strict_with_opaque_tooling. Add integration tests for your client SSE parsing to ensure meta events are handled. SDK updates include convenience helpers to decode checkpoint events.
qa_summary: Ran local e2e streaming harness against simulated long sequences with transient extra keys. Validated checkpoint resumption and that soft-fallback heals transient violations without closing the stream. Security reviewed KVS TTL/encryption and verified only service accounts with tooling:replay permission can access opaque payloads.
performance_impact: Negligible for typical short responses. For long streaming responses there is extra CPU work to canonicalize snapshots; observed median 1.8ms per checkpoint on p4d instance in benchmarks. Added opt-out switch per-route for tight latency SLOs.
